conviction_note: Near-non-result: the only company-level documents are the Q2 release, the 10-Q and two 8-Ks, all public; the filed items are a weak negative proxy on the $227m Zimmer-managed utility/infrastructure fund (utilities ETF XLU about -11% in Q3, but the fund beat XLU by ~11 points in Q2), a hurricane-free Q3 (public, partly priced), and a reaction history that sold the last fully pre-signalled beat (-3.21%); the bar is single-sourced so every size is capped small, p_up 46 on a 5.0 abs move gives -0.4 against an impact_sum of -0.6, and the two agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.50 (Q4 $0.58) from one source only, Benzinga earnings-forecasts page https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/ASIC/earnings-forecasts (seen in search snippet 2026-10-21, page 403 on fetch); FY2026 $1.91 from two analysts (tickflow, data as of 2026-08-01, https://www.tickflow.io/stock/ASIC/forecast). No company guidance: the Q2 release and the 2026-07-10 8-K give no Q3 or FY numbers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002040491/000204049126000040/asic-2026729xexx991.htm). Sources also disagree on the Q2 consensus ($0.53 vs $0.47), so the bar is UNSOURCED for sizing purposes and every finding is capped small. Note adjusted EPS equalled GAAP in Q2 ($0.67) and included $18.6m of investment gains, so the EPS bar embeds an assumption about the Zimmer fund mark; a core-only run-rate (UW income $16.0m + NII $12.7m, ~21% tax, 49.9m diluted shares) was about $0.45 in Q2.
positioning_check: Short interest ~3.3-3.4% of float per Benzinga sentiment page updated 2026-10-16 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ASIC/sentiment, via sweep row); ~4.2 days to cover per Equibles (undated, via sweep). Not a crowded short; days to cover elevated only because turnover is thin (20d avg 69,956 shares, ~$1.9m/day at $27.42). No listed options (baseline options.status no_options_market), so no skew and no implied move. Tape into the print: +4.74% over 5 days, +3.39% over 20, 4.33% below the 52-week high, 60% above the low. Sponsor (Zimmer) controls the float; no Form 144, S-3, 424B or 13D/G filings since IPO on EDGAR as of 2026-10-21 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002040491&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.finding: ASIC carries $227.3m (19% of $1,175.8m invested assets) in Zimmer-managed 'Utility & Infrastructure Investments' (Absolute Return Utility & Infrastructure Fund $215.9m, MidCap LP $11.4m) whose marks run through net income and, in Q2, through adjusted EPS (Q2 gains $18.6m, ~$0.29/share pre-tax of the $0.67); the utilities ETF XLU fell from ~$44.77 (late June) to ~$39.44 (late September), about -11% in Q3, so if the fund kept any long utility beta the Q3 mark is a drag against a $0.50 bar that assumes something near flat - a $227m fund down 3% is about -$6.8m pre-tax, roughly -$0.11/share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS $0.67 (about $0.29 of it investment gains) against $0.53 consensus and the stock fell 3.21% (2026-07-29); the pre-release of 'EPS above $0.60 vs $0.47' bought +0.5% (2026-07-10). The market has not paid for investment-driven EPS on this name, which argues the line moves the stock little in either direction.
findings.why_not_priced: One analyst-level consensus exists and nobody publishes the Zimmer fund's NAV; if the market had marked the fund to XLU, the stock would not be up 4.7% in five days and 4% from its high into the print. But the fund is labelled 'absolute return' and in Q2 it gained ~8% (realized $21.3m) while XLU fell ~3%, and in Q1 it gained ~4% while XLU rose ~10%, so the transmission is unconfirmed and the size is small.
findings.independence: XLU weekly closes from Yahoo chart API (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/XLU?interval=1wk&period1=1767225600&period2=1792540800&events=split,div, data to 2026-10-15/20) is the only proxy; it is not the fund. Q1/Q2 history from the same 10-Q cuts against the transmission. Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: The 2026 Atlantic season produced no hurricane in Q3: the NHC 2026 archive lists Arthur through Hanna as tropical storms only, and the season's first hurricane, Isaias, has advisories from 2026-10-06 to 10-11, i.e. in Q4; ASIC writes $73.3m a quarter of E&S property (Q2 +21.3%), so Q3 hurricane cat load should be light against the Q2 loss ratio of 58.5% (Q2 2025's comparison cited 'lower catastrophe activity').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No quarter on record where ASIC disclosed a cat number in the release; the Q2 release attributed a 0.5-point loss ratio rise partly to lower prior-year cats. No measured reaction to a cat surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a hurricane-free quarter is public and every P&C name benefits. What is not visible is severe convective storm (hail/wind) losses in the Midwest, which is where ASIC says it is growing property ('Project Heartland'); if the market expected a CR beat from cats the stock would carry it into the print, and it is near its high, consistent with this being mostly in.
findings.independence: Hurricane Isaias advisory dates from https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/2026/ISAIAS.shtml (same NHC source, so one finding). No peer Q3 cat figure reached (search budget exhausted).

findings.finding: This name sold its last fully signalled beat: Q2 GWP +23.4%, CR 85.9% vs 88.9%, expense ratio down 350bp, EPS $0.67 vs $0.53 consensus, and the stock fell 3.21% on the 2026-07-29 print after +0.5% on the 2026-07-10 pre-release; it now goes into Q3 up 4.74% in five days and 4.3% from its 52-week high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last six prints: -3.21, +0.50 (pre-release), -7.36, +23.60, -0.42, +5.15; 3 of 6 up; the only big up move (Feb 19, +23.6%) coincided with a $50m buyback authorization 8-K the same day.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is priced by definition; the point is the reaction function. If holders were braced for a sell-the-news print the stock would not have risen into it on thin volume.
findings.independence: Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002040491/000204049126000040/asic-2026729xexx991.htm (the beat) and the baseline's reaction history (the moves). Run-up from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Capacity to buy back: a $50m repurchase authorization from 2026-02-12 (8-K 2026-02-19) of which only ~$2.9m (142,686 shares) was used in Q2 per the 10-Q; with ~$1.9m of daily turnover the remaining ~$45m is large relative to the tape, and an acceleration or an update could accompany the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The authorization was announced with the Q4 2025 print on 2026-02-19, the day the stock rose 23.6% (not separable from the results).
findings.why_not_priced: Authorization is public; Q3 usage is not, and no 8-K or press release since September discloses it. Small because nothing says the pace changed.

findings.finding: President and Chief Underwriting Officer Chris Schenk's contract was extended to 2028-12-31 on 2026-09-04 with salary $550k -> $750k, a $1.25m 2026 target bonus and 125,658 options struck at $27.40 (Form 4 2026-09-09), retaining the underwriting lead into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September and mostly priced; it removes a key-person risk rather than adding information about Q3.

findings.finding: Related-party concentration rose with the CFO change: on 2026-07-06 the CFO was not renewed and Zimmer Partners' own CFO (Neil Adler, $200k salary) became ASIC's CFO and principal accounting officer, while $227.3m of Zimmer-managed funds plus $106.5m of loans to Zimmer affiliates are 28% of invested assets; Q3 is the second quarter closed under him.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The CFO change was disclosed with the Q2 pre-release (2026-07-10), +0.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months; only matters if the release changes related-party exposure. Near zero.
findings.independence: Investment and affiliate-loan balances from the 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040491/000204049126000045/asic-20260630.htm; shares the 10-Q with finding 1 but is a different fact (governance, not the mark).
